bridges.rationale: Bias can qualify planning estimates, but denominator validity needs local testing.
Population estimation and vaccine strategy share coverage concerns, but no campaign performance measured.
Turnover creates an immunity-maintenance issue; local vaccination cohorts not observed.
Normative guidance differentiates culling and vaccination without a local comparative trial.
WHO treats human PEP as a complementary prevention component; actual access unmeasured.
WOAH discusses roaming ownership whereas Belo reviews detection; combined survey bias is a hypothesis needing evidence.
Trend and abundance measurement differ; neither is free of sampling issues.
Exposure and PEP appear at distinct points in the human rabies prevention pathway.
Assessment and population estimates inform adaptive planning; effectiveness not established.

caveat: Second LLM agreement is not independent empirical replication or human verification. Even an entailed label is not accepted evidence.
